text: A database is an organized collection of information that allows users to store, manage, and retrieve data efficiently. The most common type is the relational database, which stores data in tables consisting of rows and columns. To interact with this data, you use SQL (Structured Query Language) to write queries, such as selecting specific records or updating values. Before building a database, careful data modeling is essential—this means designing the tables and relationships to avoid errors. Indexes are also important, as they speed up searches by allowing the system to find data without scanning every row. Alternatively, NoSQL databases store data in flexible formats like documents, which work better for unstructured information and large-scale applications.
